old_text: Before the commencement of the match two umpires shall be appointed, one for each end.
new_text: Before the commencement of the match two umpires shall be appointed: one for each end.

old_text: The ball shall weigh not less than 5½oz. nor more than 5¾oz.
new_text: The ball shall weigh not less than five ounces and a half, nor more than five ounces and three-quarters.

old_text: It shall measure not less than 9in. nor more than 9½in. in circumference.
new_text: It shall measure not less than nine inches, nor more than nine inches and one quarter in circumference.

old_text: The bat shall not exceed 4¼in. in the widest part; it shall not be more than 38in. in length.
new_text: The bat shall not exceed four inches and one-quarter in the widest part; it shall not be more than 38 inches in length.

old_text: The wickets shall be pitched opposite and parallel to each other, at a distance of 22 yards.
new_text: The wickets shall be pitched opposite and parallel to each other at a distance of 22 yards.

old_text: Each wicket shall be 8in. in width, and consist of three stumps, with two bails upon the top.
new_text: Each wicket shall be eight inches in width, and consist of three stumps, with two bails upon the top.

old_text: The stumps shall be of equal and sufficient size to prevent the ball from passing through, 27in. out of the ground.
new_text: The Stumps shall be of equal and sufficient size to prevent the ball passing through, 27 inches out of the ground.

old_text: The bails shall be each 4¼in. in length, and when in position, on the top of the stumps, shall not project more than ¾in. above them.
new_text: The bails shall be each four inches in length, and, when in position on top of the stumps, shall not project more than half-an-inch above them.

old_text: The wickets shall not be changed during the match, unless the ground between them becomes unfit for play, and then only by consent of both sides.
new_text: The wickets shall not be changed during the match unless the ground between them become unfit for play, and then only by consent of both sides.

old_text: The bowling crease shall be in a line with the stumps, 6ft. 8in. in length; the stumps in the centre, with a return crease at each end, at right angles behind the wicket.
new_text: The bowling crease shall be in a line with the stumps 6 feet 8 inches in length, the stumps in the centre, with a return crease at each end, at right angles behind the wicket.

old_text: The popping crease shall be marked 4ft. from the wicket, parallel to it, and be deemed unlimited in length.
new_text: The popping crease shall be marked four feet from the wicket, parallel to it, and deemed unlimited in length.

old_text: The ground shall not be rolled, watered, covered, mown or beaten during a match, except before the commencement of each innings and of each day’s play, when, unless the in-side object, the ground shall be swept and rolled for not more than ten minutes.
new_text: The ground shall not be rolled, watered, covered mown, or beaten during a match except before the commencement of each innings and of each day’s play, when unless the in-side object, the ground shall be swept and rolled for not more than ten minutes.

old_text: The ball must be bowled; if thrown or jerked, the umpire shall call “No ball.”
new_text: The ball must be bowled; if thrown or jerked either umpire shall call “no ball.”

old_text: If the bowler shall bowl the ball so high over or so wide of the wicket that in the opinion of the umpire it is not within reach of the striker, the umpire shall call “Wide ball.”
new_text: If the bowler shall bowl the ball so high over or so wide of the wicket, that in the opinion of the umpire it is not within reach of the striker the umpire shall call “wide ball.”

old_text: The ball shall be bowled in overs of five balls from each wicket alternately.
new_text: The ball shall be bowled in overs of six balls from each wicket alternately.

old_text: When five balls have been bowled, and the ball is finally settled in the bowler’s or wicket-keeper’s hands, the umpire shall call “Over.”
new_text: When six balls have been bowled, and the ball is finally settled in the bowler's or wicket-keeper’s hands, the umpire shall call “over.”

old_text: Neither a “no-ball” nor a “wide-ball” shall be reckoned as one of the “over.”
new_text: Neither a “no ball” nor a “wide ball” shall be reckoned as one of the over.

old_text: The bowler shall be allowed to change ends as often as he pleases, provided only that he does not bowl two overs consecutively in one innings.
new_text: The bowler may change ends as often as he pleases, provided that he shall not bowl two overs in succession in the same innings.

title_to: SCORING OFF NO BALLS AND WIDE BALLS
old_text: The striker may hit a “no-ball,” and whatever runs result shall be added to his score; but he shall not be out from a “no-ball,” unless he be run out or break laws 26, 27, 29, 30.
new_text: The striker may hit a “no ball,” and whatever runs result shall be added to his score; but he shall not be out from a “no ball” unless he be run out or break Laws 26, 27, 29 and 30.

title_to: SCORING OFF NO BALLS AND WIDE BALLS
old_text: All runs made from a “no-ball,” otherwise than from the bat, shall be scored “no-balls,” and if no runs be made one run shall be added to that score.
new_text: All runs made from a “no ball,” otherwise than from the bat, shall be scored “no balls,” and, if no run be made, one run shall be added to that score.

title_to: SCORING OFF NO BALLS AND WIDE BALLS
old_text: From a “wide-ball” as many runs as are run shall be added to the score as “wide balls,” and if no runs be otherwise obtained one run shall be so added.
new_text: From a “wide ball” as many runs as are run shall be added to that score as “wide balls,” and if no runs be otherwise obtained, one run shall be so added.

old_text: If the ball, not having been called “wide” or “no-ball,” pass the striker, without touching his bat, or person, and any runs be obtained, the umpire shall call “Bye”; but if the ball touch any part of the striker’s person (hand excepted) and any run be obtained, the umpire shall call “Leg-bye,” such runs to be scored “byes” and “leg-byes” respectively.
new_text: If the ball, not having been called “wide” or “no-ball,” pass the striker without touching his bat or person, and any runs be obtained, the umpire shall call “bye;” but if the ball touch any part of the striker’s person (hand excepted) and any run be obtained, the umpire shall call “leg-bye;” such runs to be scored “byes” and “leg-byes” respectively.

old_text: No trial ball shall be allowed to any bowler on the ground between the wickets, and when one of the batsmen is out the use of the bat shall not be allowed to any person until the next batsman shall come in.
new_text: No trial ball shall be allowed to any bowler on the ground between the wickets, and, when one of the batsmen is out the use of the bat shall not be allowed to any person until the next batsman shall come in.

old_text: The wicket shall be held to be “down” when either of the bails is struck off, or, if both bails be off, when the stump is struck out of the ground.
new_text: The wicket shall be held to be “down” when either of the bails is struck off or, if both bails be off, when a stump is struck out of the ground.

old_text: If the wicket be bowled down, even if the ball first touch the striker’s bat or person :—“Bowled.”
new_text: The striker is out if the wicket be bowled down, even if the ball first touch the striker's bat or person:

old_text: Or, if the ball, from a stroke of the bat or hand, but not the wrist, be held before it touch the ground, although it be hugged to the body of the catcher:—“Caught.”
new_text: Or, if a ball, from a stroke of the bat or hand, but not the wrist be held before it touch the ground, although it be hugged to the body of the catcher:—“Caught.”

old_text: Or, if in playing at the ball, provided it be not touched by the bat or hand, the striker be out of his ground, and the wicket be put down by the wicket-keeper with the ball or with hand or arm, with ball in hand:—“Stumped.”
new_text: Or, if in playing at the ball, provided it be not touched by the bat or hand the striker be out of his ground, and the wicket be put down by the wicket-keeper with the ball or with the hand or arm, with ball in hand:—“Stumped.”

old_text: Or, if the ball be struck, or be stopped by any part of his person, and he wilfully strike it again, except it be done for the purpose of guarding his wicket, which he may do with his bat, or any part of his person, except his hands:—“Hit the ball twice.”
new_text: Or, if the ball be struck or be stopped by any part of his person, and he wilfully strike it again, except it be done for the purpose of guarding his wicket, which he may do with his bat or any part of his person, except his hands:—“Hit the ball twice.”

old_text: If in running, or at any other time, while the ball is in play, he be out of his ground, and his wicket be struck down by the ball after touching any fieldsman, or by the hand or arm, with ball in hand, of any fieldsman:—“Run out.”
new_text: Either batsman is out if in running, or at any other time, while the ball is in play, he be out of his ground, and his wicket be struck down by the ball after touching any fieldsman, or by the hand or arm (with ball in hand) of any fieldsman:—“Run out.”

old_text: Or, if he touch with his hands or take up the ball while in play, unless at the request of the opposite side:—“Handled the ball.”
new_text: Or, if he touch with his hands or take up the ball while in play, unless at the request of the opposite side:— “Handled the ball.”

old_text: Or, if he wilfully obstruct any fieldsman:—“Obstructing the field.”
new_text: Or if he wilfully obstruct any fieldsman:—Obstructing the field.’

old_text: If the batsmen have crossed each other, he that runs for the wicket which is put down is out; if they have not crossed, he that has left the wicket which is put down is out.
new_text: If the batsman have crossed each other, he that runs for the wicket which is put down is out; if they have not crossed, he that has left the wicket which is put down is out.

old_text: The striker being caught, no run shall be scored.
new_text: The striker being caught no run shall be scored.

old_text: If a ball in play cannot be found or recovered, any fieldsman may call “lost ball,” when the ball shall be “dead”; six runs shall be added to the score, but if more than six runs have been run before “lost ball” has been called, as many runs as have been run shall be scored.
new_text: If a ball in play cannot be found or recovered, any fieldsman may call “lost-ball,” when the ball shall be “dead;” six runs shall be added to the score; but if more than six runs have been run before “lost ball” has been called as many runs as have been run shall be scored.

old_text: After the ball shall have been finally settled in the wicket-keeper’s or bowler’s hand it shall be “dead”; but when the bowler is about to deliver the ball, if the batsman at his wicket be out of his ground before actual delivery, the said bowler may run him out; but if the bowler throw at that wicket and any run result, it shall be scored “no-ball.”

old_text: A substitute shall be allowed to field or run between wickets for any player who may during the match be incapacitated from illness or injury, but for no other reason, except with the consent of the opposite side.
new_text: A substitute shall be allowed to field or run between wickets for any player who may, during the match be incapacitated from illness or injury, but for no other reason except with the consent of the opposite side.

old_text: In all cases where a substitute shall be allowed, the consent of the opposite side shall be obtained as to the person to act as substitute and the place in the field which he shall take.
new_text: In all cases where a substitute shall be allowed, the consent of the opposite side shall be obtained as to a person to act as a substitute, and the place in the field which he shall take.

old_text: If the striker be out of his ground while the ball is in play, that wicket which he has left may be put down and the striker given out, although the other batsman may have made good the ground at that end, and the striker and his substitute at the other end.
new_text: If the striker be out of his ground while the ball is in play, that wicket which he has left may be put down and the striker given out, although the other batsman may have made good the ground at the end, and the striker and his substitute at the other end.

old_text: A batsman is liable to be out for any infringement of the laws by his substitute.
new_text: A batsman is liable to be put out for any infringe ment of the laws by his substitute.

old_text: The fieldsman may stop the ball with any part of his person, but if he wilfully stop it otherwise the ball shall be “dead,” and five runs added to the score.
new_text: The fieldsman may stop the ball with any part of his person, but if he wilfully stop it otherwise, the ball shall be “dead” and five runs added to the score; whatever runs may have been made, five only shall be added.

old_text: If he shall take the ball for the purpose of stumping before it has passed the wicket, or if he shall incommode the striker by any noise, or motion, or if any part of his person be over or before the wicket, the striker shall not be out, excepting under laws 26, 27, 28, 29, and 30.

old_text: The umpires are the sole judges of fair or unfair play, of the fitness of the ground, the weather, and the light for play; all disputes shall be determined by them, and if they disagree the actual state of things shall continue.

old_text: When they shall call “Play,” the side refusing to play shall lose the match.

old_text: If either batsman run a short run, the umpire shall call “One short,” and the run shall not be scored.
new_text: If either batsman run a short run the umpire shall call “one short,” and the run shall not be scored.

old_text: After the umpire has called “Over,” the ball is “dead,” but an appeal may be made as to whether either batsman is out; such appeal, however, shall not be made after the delivery of the next ball, nor after any cessation of play.

old_text: One wicket shall be pitched, as in Law 6, with a bowling stump opposite to it, at a distance of 22 yards. The bowling crease shall be in a line with the bowling stump, and drawn according to Law 7. When there shall be less than five players on a side, bounds shall be placed 22 yards each in a line from the off and leg stump. The ball must be hit before the bounds to entitle the striker to a run, which run cannot be obtained unless he touch the bowling stump or crease in a line with his bat, or some part of his person, or go beyond them, and return to the popping crease. When the striker shall hit the ball, one of his feet must be on the ground behind the popping crease, otherwise the umpire shall call “No hit,” and no run shall be scored. When there shall be less than five players on a side, neither byes, leg-byes, nor overthrows shall be allowed, nor shall the striker be caught out behind the wicket, nor stumped. The fieldsman must return the ball so that it shall cross the ground between the wicket and the bowling stump, or between the bowling stump and the bounds; the striker may run till the ball be so returned. After the striker shall have made one run, if he start again he must touch the bowling stump or crease and turn before the ball cross the ground to entitle him to another. The striker shall be entitled to three runs for lost ball, and the same number for ball wilfully stopped by a fieldsman otherwise than with any part of his person. When there shall be more than four players on a side there shall be no bounds. All hits, byes, leg-byes, and overthrows shall then be allowed. There shall be no restriction as to the ball being bowled in overs, but no more than one minute shall be allowed between each ball.
